properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 25 at 3:54PM MDT until September 25 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Jefferson County in central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 600 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 354 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 1.25 inchES of rain has
fallen.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Clear Creek, Tucker Gulch, Ralston Creek and Van Bibber Creek.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Southwestern Arvada, western Wheat Ridge, northwestern Golden and
White Ranch Open Space.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 25 at 3:36PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 336 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from near Rocky Flats to near Tiny Town, or
extending from 20 miles northwest of Denver to 19 miles southwest of
Denver, moving east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Western Denver, Lakewood, southwestern Thornton, Arvada,
Westminster, southwestern Broomfield, northwestern Highlands Ranch,
Littleton, Northglenn, Englewood, Wheat Ridge, Golden, Federal
Heights, Sheridan, Morrison, Red Rocks Park, Idledale, Indian Hills
and Tiny Town.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 25 at 2:21PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

In the wake of today's precipitation, our attention will turn to the
Eastern Pacific. Tropical moisture is anticipated to spread across
the Desert Southwest early next week, drawing moisture from a pair of
Hurricanes; Odalys and Polo. The forecast becomes increasing complex
due to a closed low currently forecast to drive across the Southwest
CONUS as Hurricane Polo approaches the Baja California Peninsula.
Strong southerly winds ahead of the low are expected to pull tropical
moisture towards eastern Utah and western Colorado as early as Monday
morning. The challenge and uncertainty in our precipitation forecast
increase as the week progresses and the low traverses our southern
States. Excessive rainfall is most probable over AZ and NM, attm, but
the northerly extent poses a threat to our southern San Juan river
basins. Current forecasts suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain over Monday
morning through Wednesday. At face value, rivers and tributaries will
see a bump up due to said moisture. However, localized heavier
amounts could result in minor flooding across the southern San Juan
foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been observed over the
previous 7 days. However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts
(i.e. above 90th percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action
stage to minor flooding. Most probable basins to see significant
rises include; the Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito
Creek, and the Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Please continue to monitor the forecast as these systems
evolve. Especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in
the southwest quadrant of the forecast area.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 25 at 2:07PM MDT until September 25 at 5:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Lee and P-L Gulch burn scar in...
South Central Rio Blanco County in northwestern Colorado...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

* At 207 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Lee and P-L Gulch Burn Scars. Between 0.3 and
0.5 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 2 to
2.5 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.3 to 0.8
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Lee and P-L Gulch Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Lee and P-L Gulch Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Rio Blanco County.
